summary:
Implemented the terminal window title feature in the repository, without committing and without running tests or Black (per instructions).

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 to ControlType (no renumbering) and Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the SET_WINDOW_TITLE formatter emitting ESC ] 0 ; title BEL with the title unmodified; added Control.title(title), returning an unstyled control holding one title control, with docstring summary and Args entry.
- rich/console.py: added Console.set_window_title(title) -> bool. Buffers the control only when is_terminal, returns True if written and False otherwise, never catches exceptions, and its docstring notes that Rich cannot restore titles.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: added an elif branch that calls term.set_title(title) once per title control, in order, using its second item.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an Unreleased "Added" bullet linking pull request 2200.
- Tests added: test_set_window_title in tests/test_console.py (skipped on win32), test_control_title in tests/test_control.py, and test_control_set_window_title in tests/test_windows_renderer.py (Windows only, mocked wrapper, expects set_title("Hello, world!")).

Verification: no tests were run. I checked by reading that no added Python line exceeds 88 characters. Black formatting was not run.

Choices: text-mode output needed no extra code because the existing _render_buffer already emits control segment text and drops it when not a terminal.
